channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [8] Field-angle-resolved heat transport in UTe2: determination of nodal positions in the superconducting order parameter
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: P. J. Hirschfeld, Johnpierre Paglione

Authors: Ian M. Hayes, Elliot Fang, Shanta R. Saha, Vivek Mishra, P. J. Hirschfeld, Johnpierre Paglione

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental characterization of gap symmetry in the high-profile unconventional superconductor UTe2.

Tags: #UTe2 #superconductivity #transport

Abstract: Determining the gap symmetry of superconducting phases in UTe2 remains a central challenge. Here, the authors use field-angle-dependent thermal conductivity and theoretical analysis to identify b-axis point nodes in the low-field state, consistent with a B2u order parameter.
